differences.title: 1. DATA MODEL
differences.leftDesc: RocketDB stores data in columns, optimizing analytical queries by reading only necessary data. This is ideal for aggregations and complex analytics on large datasets.
differences.rightDesc: RocksDB stores data as a collection of key-value pairs. It's designed for fast reads and writes of individual records, making it suitable for transactional workloads.

differences.title: 2. PRIMARY USE CASE
differences.leftDesc: Optimized for Online Analytical Processing (OLAP) workloads, enabling rapid execution of complex queries over large volumes of data for business intelligence.
differences.rightDesc: Designed for Online Transactional Processing (OLTP) and embedded use cases, offering high-performance data retrieval and storage for application backends.

differences.title: 3. MEMORY MANAGEMENT
differences.leftDesc: RocketDB leverages its in-memory architecture for extreme query speeds. It can spill to disk but prioritizes main memory for performance-critical operations.
differences.rightDesc: RocksDB is primarily disk-oriented, using an LSM-tree structure. It aggressively caches hot data in memory but is designed to handle datasets larger than RAM.

differences.title: 4. ARCHITECTURE
differences.leftDesc: Built as a columnar database engine, enabling efficient vectorization and compression for analytical queries. It offers specialized query optimization for this structure.
differences.rightDesc: Implements a Log-Structured Merge-tree (LSM-tree) data structure, optimizing write performance by buffering writes in memory before flushing to disk.

differences.title: 5. QUERY LANGUAGE
differences.leftDesc: Provides a powerful SQL interface for complex data manipulation and querying, making it familiar and accessible to a wide range of data professionals.
differences.rightDesc: Accessed through a C++ API (with bindings for other languages). It offers methods like Put, Get, Delete, and Scan for direct data operations.

differences.title: 6. SCALABILITY
differences.leftDesc: Primarily scales vertically by adding more RAM and CPU resources to a single instance, focusing on maximizing performance on powerful hardware.
differences.rightDesc: Designed to be embedded within applications, scaling with the application instances. It excels in single-node scenarios or distributed with external coordination.

differences.title: 7. DATA COMPRESSION
differences.leftDesc: Utilizes advanced columnar compression algorithms (e.g., RLE, dictionary encoding) tailored for repeating values within columns, significantly reducing storage footprint.
differences.rightDesc: Applies compression to data blocks on disk, often using algorithms like Snappy or Zstd. This provides general-purpose compression for the underlying storage.
